summary: Johannes Schneider is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Magister at the University of Marburg (1986–1992). He held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the University of Munich, and the Bavarian and Göttingen Academies of Sciences and Humanities.

Johannes Schubert was a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Leipzig and under scholars including Conrady, Francke, Franke, and Weller. He worked at Leipzig University Library (~1927–1954) and held professorial posts at Leipzig (1934–1945, 1960–1962).

John A. Ardussi is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from the Australian National University (attested 1977) and studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie. He worked as an aeronautical engineer at ELDEC and researcher at CNRS.

John Alexander Jorgensen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner by 1979, later serving as an adjunct associate professor there and senior lecturer at Griffith University.

John Alexander Stewart, a linguist educated at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1905–1933). From ~1933 to 1948, he was Reader in Burmese at the University of London and held a post at SOAS.

John Allan was an Indologist and historian who studied at the universities of Edinburgh and Leipzig. He was Keeper of the Department of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1931) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Amherst College, the University of Tübingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).
John B. Carman is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 1999) and director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

John B. Cobb Jr. is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont Graduate University and Claremont School of Theology (attested 1989).

John Borthwick Gilchrist was a linguist and Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, headed Fort William College (1800–1804), and became the first Professor of Hindustani at University College London (~1828–1831).
John Bray is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang and held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Brockington is an Indologist who spent his career at the University of Edinburgh, where he served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1987) and Professor of Sanskrit (attested 1998–2003).

John Brough was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Keith and Bailey. He was Professor of Sanskrit at London/SOAS (1948–1967) and later Professor at the University of Cambridge (1967–1984).

John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia by 1982. He later served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).
John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as a professor at the University of St Andrews from ~1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal College of Music and the University of Oxford. He held posts at Deccan College (~1958–1959) and SOAS University of London (~1953–1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a Professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987–1990, 2000).

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He spent his career at the University of North Florida, where he served as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790–1797). In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classical historian educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked for the Oxford Latin Dictionary (~1946–1952) before serving as Reader in Classics at the University of Cambridge (1969–1984).
